goal: Make the stored preview dispatch instruction name its dispatch mode, so an operator reading the instruction can tell which modes its route must be dispatched with. The producer attaches mode_sequence to the ready record AFTER both digests are taken, deliberately leaving ready_id and manifest_digest unchanged; mode_sequence is carried for a later phase and no validator refuses a manifest that omits it today. WHAT mode_sequence DOES NOT DO: it does not by itself stop an ordinary or merged stored instruction from being dispatched at the workflow's mode input default, which is dry-run. mode_sequence has no consumer outside its producers (orchestrator-flow/reconcile.mjs:49 and manage-migration-author-lanes.mjs:2084) and the tests; nothing reads it back off a stored record and refuses a dispatch on its value. For the ordinary and merged routes a dry-run is a REQUIRED first phase and stays legal, so there is no lane to close there. The only lane this change actually closes is the historical one, and it is closed by the workflow's historical apply-only guard, not by mode_sequence: a historical dispatch left at the mode input default is REFUSED by name, instead of running neither the recovery proof nor a bounded dry-run and reporting green and empty. An earlier generation of this goal text implied mode_sequence itself prevented a silent dry-run; that was an overstatement and is corrected here. Two things are enforced. The production gate's bare test -n checks gain named REFUSED messages instead of dying with only an exit code. And re-preparing a preview-ready identity written before this change still converges. Generation 3 attempted that second behaviour by narrowing the STORED digest to ready identity, which was wrong and was rejected by two independent reviews: consumers re-derive sha256(canonicalJson(<stored record>)) from the record they read back (manage-migration-author-lanes.mjs:2094), so narrowing the writer repaired the 117 pre-change refs by making every NEWLY written ref unreadable and fail-closing historical terminalization. The shipped fix keeps the stored digest over the whole record and instead judges OCCUPANCY on identity, comparing both sides with mode_sequence stripped, so a pre-change ref converges without changing what any reader recomputes. KNOWN CONSEQUENCE OF JUDGING OCCUPANCY ON IDENTITY, accepted deliberately and recorded here rather than left for a reviewer to rediscover: because persistInitialReady now compares readyIdentityDigest and no longer compares the stored bytes, a ref whose stored DIGEST is corrupted while its identity is otherwise unchanged no longer fails at persistInitialReady. It converges there, and the corruption surfaces later, at historical terminalization, where terminalizeHistoricalPreviewReady re-derives the whole-record digest and refuses on the mismatch (manage-migration-author-lanes.mjs:2094). Detection of that corruption is therefore DEFERRED from the write path to the terminal path, not lost. That deferral is the price of letting the 117 pre-change refs converge, and it must not be 'fixed' by narrowing the stored digest: that is precisely the generation-3 defect two reviews rejected, and the whole-record stored digest has to stay.
